Hindi - 24.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: Michael Kim shoots 59(!!!) for new course record | 3M Open | Round 2 | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
Michael Kim shoots 59(!!!) for new course record | 3M Open | Round 2 | 2026 In the second round of the 2026 3M Open, Michael Kim makes 12 birdies and zero bogeys for a course-record 59! It marks the 16th sub-60 score in PGA TOUR history. 

His putt on 18 makes the longest putt for 59 in PGA TOUR history! 

The PGA TOUR returns to Minnesota this week for the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities, with just three events remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs. As the Regular Season draws to a close, valuable FedExCup points are up for grabs as players make their final push to secure a place inside the top 70. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler headlines the field in his tournament debut after finishing T4 at The Open Championship, while recent Genesis Scottish Open winner Tom Kim returns looking to bounce back from a missed cut at Royal Birkdale. Defending champion Kurt Kitayama is back in Minnesota aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the 3M Open title after claiming victory with a closing 65 last year. The FedExCup Playoff race also takes centre stage, with players including Jason Day, Brian Harman, Brandt Snedeker and Tony Finau all looking to climb inside the top 70 before the postseason begins. Rising amateur star and reigning NCAA champion Preston Stout is also in the field after a string of impressive performances this summer. With 500 FedExCup points available and the postseason fast approaching, the 3M Open once again promises a pivotal week at TPC Twin Cities as the battle for Playoff qualification intensifies.

videos.title: 5 Blood Test Results You Should Never Ignore After 40  |  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
5 Blood Test Results You Should Never Ignore After 40  |  Dr. Mandell In this video, we break down five important blood tests that may help reveal hidden cardiovascular risk after age 40, even when you feel well and have no obvious symptoms. The first is the standard lipid panel, which measures LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. LDL carries cholesterol through the bloodstream, and when too many cholesterol-containing particles enter the artery wall, they can contribute to plaque formation over time. High LDL usually causes no direct symptoms, which is why testing matters. The second test is apolipoprotein B, pronounced “ap-oh-lip-oh-PRO-teen B,” or simply “A-poe-B.” ApoB helps estimate the number of potentially artery-damaging particles in the blood. Two people can have the same LDL cholesterol level but very different numbers of particles, and the person with more particles may have greater cardiovascular risk. ApoB can be especially useful when triglycerides are high, diabetes or metabolic syndrome is present, or the standard cholesterol panel does not seem to tell the whole story. The third test is lipoprotein(a), pronounced “lip-oh-PRO-teen little a,” or “L-P-little-a.” Lp(a) is largely inherited and may increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and aortic valve disease, even when routine cholesterol numbers look acceptable. Most people with elevated Lp(a) have no symptoms, so family history of early heart disease can be an important clue. The fourth test is hemoglobin A1C, often reviewed along with fasting glucose. A1C reflects your average blood sugar over approximately the previous two to three months. Chronically elevated glucose can damage the inner lining of blood vessels, promote inflammation and oxidative stress, and increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, kidney disease, nerve damage, and eye problems. Prediabetes often causes no symptoms, although higher blood sugar may lead to increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds, recurring infections, numbness or tingling, or darkened skin around the neck or underarms. The fifth area is kidney function, including creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate, called eGFR. A urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio may also be helpful because it can reveal damage to the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys. The heart and kidneys are closely connected, and high blood pressure and diabetes can damage both systems. Early kidney disease is often silent, while later symptoms may include ankle swelling, foamy urine, fatigue, itching, nausea, changes in urination, or shortness of breath. We also discuss high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, or hsCRP, as a possible bonus test for selected people. hsCRP measures a signal of inflammation, but it does not diagnose blocked arteries and can also rise because of infection, injury, arthritis, obesity, dental disease, and other conditions. These tests do not diagnose heart disease by themselves, and no single number can predict with certainty whether someone will have a heart attack. Your healthcare professional must interpret them together with your age, blood pressure, family history, smoking status, medications, activity level, nutrition, sleep, waist size, blood sugar, kidney health, and sometimes imaging such as a coronary artery calcium scan. Know your LDL, HDL, and triglycerides, ask whether ApoB could provide additional information, ask whether you have ever had Lp(a) measured, understand your A1C, creatinine, eGFR, and urine albumin, and discuss whether hsCRP or additional cardiovascular testing is appropriate for you. Never ignore new chest pressure, severe shortness of breath, fainting, cold sweating, sudden weakness, facial drooping, trouble speaking, or pain spreading into the arm, jaw, shoulder, or back, because those symptoms require immediate medical evaluation.

*********************************

24.07.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: The ONLY 2 Ab Exercises You Need
videos.summary_source_text:
The ONLY 2 Ab Exercises You Need If you want visible, well-developed six pack abs, you do not need an endless list of ab exercises. You need to train the abs through the two primary movement patterns that matter most and choose exercises that match your current strength level.

GET A FLAT STOMACH IN 22 DAYS (FREE) - https://www.athleanx.com/flatstomach

In this ATHLEAN-X Short, Jeff Cavaliere explains why just two exercises for abs can be enough to build a stronger, more defined midsection. The key is selecting one top-down ab exercise and one bottom-up ab exercise. Together, these movements train the rectus abdominis by bringing the chest toward the pelvis and the pelvis toward the chest.

Top-down ab exercises emphasize the portion of the movement where the rib cage moves toward the pelvis. Bottom-up exercises reverse the action by bringing the pelvis toward the chest. Training both directions gives you a more complete ab workout without wasting time on dozens of random exercises.

Your exercise choices should also reflect your ability level. An exercise that is too easy will not provide enough overload, while one that is too advanced may cause you to lose control and compensate with other muscles. Start with the variation you can perform correctly, then progress as your abs become stronger.

BOTTOM-UP AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Reverse corkscrew with bent knees
Intermediate: Reverse corkscrew with straight legs
Advanced: Hanging corkscrew

TOP-DOWN AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Upper circle crunch
Intermediate: Power over
Advanced: Cable crunch pulldown

Choose one exercise from each category and perform 2 to 3 hard sets of each. Focus on controlled repetitions, a strong abdominal contraction, and taking the target muscles close to failure. Avoid rushing through the reps or turning the movement into momentum-based hip flexor work.

This approach works because effective six pack exercises do not need to be complicated. Your abs respond to tension, progressive overload, proper exercise selection, and consistent effort just like every other muscle group. As your strength improves, move to a harder variation so the workout for abs continues to produce results.

Of course, no ab workout can reveal a six pack if body fat levels remain too high. You can build stronger abdominal muscles through training, but getting a flat stomach and making those abs visible also requires nutrition that supports your goal. That usually means maintaining an appropriate calorie intake, eating enough protein, and staying consistent long enough to reduce excess body fat.

You cannot out-train a consistently poor diet. The most effective plan for anyone wondering how to get abs combines direct ab training with smart nutrition, resistance training, and enough daily activity to support fat loss. The exercises build the muscle. Your overall diet and training plan determine how clearly that muscle can be seen.

So, how many exercises do you need for a six pack? Start with two. Pick one top-down movement and one bottom-up movement, use the variation that fits your ability, and train each with purpose. When those exercises become too easy, progress to the next level rather than adding more low-quality volume.

Whether your goal is six pack abs, 6 pack abs, a flatter stomach, or simply a stronger core, the answer is not doing hundreds of careless crunches every day. It is choosing better ab exercises, performing them with control, progressively challenging the muscles, and supporting your training with a nutrition plan that keeps body fat in check.

If you want visible, well-developed six pack abs, you do not need an endless list of ab exercises. You need to train the abs through the two primary movement patterns that matter most and choose exercises that match your current strength level.

GET A FLAT STOMACH IN 22 DAYS (FREE) - https://www.athleanx.com/flatstomach

In this ATHLEAN-X Short, Jeff Cavaliere explains why just two exercises for abs can be enough to build a stronger, more defined midsection. The key is selecting one top-down ab exercise and one bottom-up ab exercise. Together, these movements train the rectus abdominis by bringing the chest toward the pelvis and the pelvis toward the chest.

Top-down ab exercises emphasize the portion of the movement where the rib cage moves toward the pelvis. Bottom-up exercises reverse the action by bringing the pelvis toward the chest. Training both directions gives you a more complete ab workout without wasting time on dozens of random exercises.

Your exercise choices should also reflect your ability level. An exercise that is too easy will not provide enough overload, while one that is too advanced may cause you to lose control and compensate with other muscles. Start with the variation you can perform correctly, then progress as your abs become stronger.

BOTTOM-UP AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Reverse corkscrew with bent knees
Intermediate: Reverse corkscrew with straight legs
Advanced: Hanging corkscrew

TOP-DOWN AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Upper circle crunch
Intermediate: Power over
Advanced: Cable crunch pulldown

Choose one exercise from each category and perform 2 to 3 hard sets of each. Focus on controlled repetitions, a strong abdominal contraction, and taking the target muscles close to failure. Avoid rushing through the reps or turning the movement into momentum-based hip flexor work.

This approach works because effective six pack exercises do not need to be complicated. Your abs respond to tension, progressive overload, proper exercise selection, and consistent effort just like every other muscle group. As your strength improves, move to a harder variation so the workout for abs continues to produce results.

Of course, no ab workout can reveal a six pack if body fat levels remain too high. You can build stronger abdominal muscles through training, but getting a flat stomach and making those abs visible also requires nutrition that supports your goal. That usually means maintaining an appropriate calorie intake, eating enough protein, and staying consistent long enough to reduce excess body fat.

You cannot out-train a consistently poor diet. The most effective plan for anyone wondering how to get abs combines direct ab training with smart nutrition, resistance training, and enough daily activity to support fat loss. The exercises build the muscle. Your overall diet and training plan determine how clearly that muscle can be seen.

So, how many exercises do you need for a six pack? Start with two. Pick one top-down movement and one bottom-up movement, use the variation that fits your ability, and train each with purpose. When those exercises become too easy, progress to the next level rather than adding more low-quality volume.

Whether your goal is six pack abs, 6 pack abs, a flatter stomach, or simply a stronger core, the answer is not doing hundreds of careless crunches every day. It is choosing better ab exercises, performing them with control, progressively challenging the muscles, and supporting your training with a nutrition plan that keeps body fat in check.

23.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

This Move Sets Up Kucherov’s Nasty Assist The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

OpenAI just admitted two of its own AI models broke out of a locked testing sandbox and reached into a rival company's live infrastructure to win a benchmark. That's the headline. But it's not the whole story.

In this video I go through three stories that all broke within 48 hours of each other — and why they're really the same story wearing three different names:

🚀 Elon Musk says SpaceX's proprietary engineering data will train xAI's next Grok model

videos.title: Put a Fennel Seed Under Your Tongue for 5 Minutes… Here’s What Happens | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Put a Fennel Seed Under Your Tongue for 5 Minutes… Here’s What Happens | Dr. Mandell Place one tiny fennel seed under your tongue for five minutes and notice how quickly your mouth begins to respond. As saliva softens the seed, natural aromatic oils—especially anethole—are gradually released, creating fennel’s familiar sweet, slightly licorice-like flavor. These compounds stimulate taste receptors and sensory nerves in the mouth, while the salivary glands may begin producing more moisture. Saliva helps lubricate the mouth, protect tooth enamel, begin the digestion of certain foods, wash away small food particles, and temporarily reduce dryness or unpleasant taste. As you breathe through your nose, the aroma can travel from the back of the mouth into the nasal passages, making the flavor seem surprisingly strong through a process called retronasal smell. Taste and aroma may also help trigger the early, anticipatory phase of digestion, where the brain signals the mouth, stomach, and digestive system to prepare for food. This may help explain why fennel seeds have traditionally been chewed after meals in many cultures. Holding one seed under the tongue is not a cure, detox, or treatment for digestive disease, but it may be a simple sensory ritual that encourages slower breathing, greater awareness, more saliva, fresher-feeling breath, and a mindful pause after eating. After five minutes, remove the seed or chew it slowly for a stronger release of flavor. Use only one small seed, remain upright, never try this while lying down or falling asleep, and stop immediately if you notice burning, coughing, swelling, irritation, or difficulty breathing. Avoid fennel if you have a known allergy to fennel or related plants, and speak with your healthcare professional before using concentrated fennel products for medical purposes.

During Round 1 at the 2026 3M Open, Jake Knapp nearly makes a hole-in-one from 171 yards out on the Par fourth hole.

As the Regular Season draws to a close, valuable FedExCup points are up for grabs as players make their final push to secure a place inside the top 70. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler headlines the field in his tournament debut after finishing T4 at The Open Championship, while recent Genesis Scottish Open winner Tom Kim returns looking to bounce back from a missed cut at Royal Birkdale. Defending champion Kurt Kitayama is back in Minnesota aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the 3M Open title after claiming victory with a closing 65 last year. The FedExCup Playoff race also takes centre stage, with players including Jason Day, Brian Harman, Brandt Snedeker and Tony Finau all looking to climb inside the top 70 before the postseason begins. Rising amateur star and reigning NCAA champion Preston Stout is also in the field after a string of impressive performances this summer. With 500 FedExCup points available and the postseason fast approaching, the 3M Open once again promises a pivotal week at TPC Twin Cities as the battle for Playoff qualification intensifies.

videos.title: Robertson signs, Greaves avoids arbitration, and Kane returns to Chicago ft. David Pagnotta
videos.summary_source_text:
Robertson signs, Greaves avoids arbitration, and Kane returns to Chicago ft. David Pagnotta On today’s episode of The Sheet, Jeff Marek is joined by David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period and Daily Faceoff. The Jason Robertson saga is over! The Stars have signed the three-time 40 goal scorer to a one-year deal worth $12 million that will walk up to unrestricted free agency next July.

The Columbus Blue Jackets also made headlines, avoiding arbitration with goaltender Jet Greaves. The 25-year old netminder will be under contract in Columbus for three more years at a $5 million AAV. What does this mean for CBJ's other RFAs in Cole Sillinger and Adam Fantilli? Jeff and Dave discuss.

The final piece of contract news this morning came from Chicago, as Patrick Kane will return to the Blackhawks for his 20th NHL season. The future Hall of Famer spent his first 16 years in the league with Chicago, winning 3 Stanley Cups with the Hawks. He's back in the Windy City for two more seasons after signing as a free agent.

videos.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash vs 3.5 Flash: The Benchmarks Are Real, The Prompting Gap Is Bigger
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 3.6 Flash vs 3.5 Flash: The Benchmarks Are Real, The Prompting Gap Is Bigger Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
Gemini 3.6 Flash just replaced 3.5 Flash as Google's default fast-tier model — and everyone's covering the launch, almost nobody's covering what actually determines whether you notice the upgrade: how you prompt it.

In this video, I break down two things:

1️⃣ The real benchmark comparison — what Google's own DeepMind numbers show on DeepSWE, OSWorld-Verified, and GDPval-AA, versus what Artificial Analysis's independent Intelligence Index actually confirms. Spoiler: the story is more nuanced than the launch headlines.

2️⃣ A practical prompting guide built specifically around what changed in this model — multi-step staging, context-rich debugging prompts, built-in self-checks, and knowing when NOT to over-structure a simple ask.

Covered in this video:

What's confirmed vs. what's still just a Google claim
Gemini 3.6 Flash pricing vs 3.5 Flash (input/output token costs)
Real before/after prompt examples for coding and agentic tasks
Why the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score didn't move
Who should actually test this model this week — and who shouldn't bother yet
How Flash Cyber and 3.5 Flash-Lite fit into this same release (full breakdown coming next video)

If you're building on Gemini for real production work, this is the 12 minutes that decides whether you get better output tonight or leave performance on the table for weeks.

🔔 Subscribe for the next video, going deep on Flash Cyber, the restricted government-only model from this same release.
💬 Drop a comment: have you run 3.6 Flash against 3.5 Flash on your own workload yet? Does the gap match Google's claims?

videos.summary_source_text:
What Happens to Your Body When You Eat One Meal a Day for 30 Days What would happen if you ate one meal a day for 30 days? Discover the benefits of intermittent fasting, how autophagy works, and what one meal a day can do to help reset your body.

0:00 One meal a day diet for 30 days
1:52 One meal a day intermittent fasting
3:16 Intermittent fasting benefits
3:59 One meal a day, day-by-day
5:23 BDNF 
6:12 One meal a day vs. three meals a day
8:15 What to eat on one meal a day
9:05 More one meal a day diet tips

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4ffUxCb

Keep watching to learn more about the benefits of fasting. 
▶️ https://youtu.be/daFxYFmUH-w
▶️ https://youtu.be/JhRqDqbyJ9o
▶️ https://youtu.be/aE1O5dG2MZE

Check out this article to learn more about the benefits of eating one meal a day, every other day: https://drbrg.co/4wXm551

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Many people eat three meals a day, but this may not be the best approach for everyone. After about 12–16 hours of fasting, glycogen stores become depleted, and your body begins burning more fat. At around 16 hours of fasting, autophagy increases as your body starts recycling old and damaged proteins, with continued activity in the liver, muscles, and brain.

Millions of people around the world practice intermittent fasting. Research has found improvements in body weight, waist circumference, triglycerides, and cholesterol markers during this period.

The first few days of a one meal a day (OMAD) diet are often the most challenging as your body adapts to using ketones for fuel. By days 4–7, many people find hunger and cravings improve as their bodies become more efficient at burning fat. Intermittent fasting also increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which supports brain health.

As intermittent fasting continues, growth hormone levels increase, supporting muscle, tendon, and ligament repair. A one meal a day diet may not be the best approach for everyone, including some postmenopausal women.

videos.title: Antidepressants Cause Weak Bones?
videos.summary_source_text:
Antidepressants Cause Weak Bones? Do Antidepressants Weaken Your Bones? 🦴 

The answer is: maybe—but it's complicated.

Studies have found that people taking antidepressants, especially SSRIs, have a higher risk of fractures and, in some cases, lower bone density.

But here's the catch...

About 1 in 6 adult women in the U.S. take antidepressants. Depression itself is also linked with lower physical activity, poorer nutrition, more inflammation, muscle loss, and a greater risk of falls. Any—or all—of these could contribute to weaker bones.

Researchers are still debating how much of the risk comes from the medication versus the underlying condition.

The takeaway? If you're taking an antidepressant, get a DEXA scan, talk to you doctor, and do your best to do all the usual bone-health promoting things such as:  

• Strength training
•  Eat enough protein and calcium
•  Get adequate vitamin D

PMID: 38863057

22.07.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Hindi - 22.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.summary_source_text:
Why the Robertson Contract is Really an 8 Year Deal | Are Teams Less Interested in Naming a Captain? Dallas Stars lock up Jason Robertson with a 1-year, $12 million deal—does this short-term agreement foreshadow a decade of Avalanche headaches? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the real motive behind this “bridge” contract, the cap implications, and why all signs point to a mega-extension as soon as January 1st. With Dallas poised to retain their offensive powerhouse and $41 million in cap space next season, how will this affect Central Division rivals like the Colorado Avalanche?

The hosts spotlight how Robertson’s decision compares to former Avalanche star Mikko Rantanen’s exit and explore whether this contract model could set a new NHL trend as the salary cap climbs. Plus, they tackle the shifting significance of captaincy in the NHL, teams going leaderless, and what this means for the Colorado Avalanche’s leadership structure. Can the Avalanche stay competitive with Robertson locked in Dallas for years to come?

videos.title: Ryan Fox wins The Open, 2026 Major Season Reactions | The Drop
videos.summary_source_text:
Ryan Fox wins The Open, 2026 Major Season Reactions | The Drop The Drop wraps up the 2026 major season with a reaction to Ryan Fox’s win at The Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. We’ll examine the importance of achieving this career highlight and how impressive it was to watch him get it done. After giving Fox his flowers, the show dives into some of the other key storylines from England – including an assessment of Scottie Scheffler’s major season, the most surprising result of The Open and a discussion on the rules of golf and how penalties are conveyed to players during the course of a tournament. Later in the show, Oklahoma State’s Preston Stout – who was the individual medalist at the 2026 NCAA Tournament – joins us to be awarded the top spot on the preseason PGA TOUR University Ranking sponsored by Huntington Bank. The rising senior talks about his accomplishments in college, the honor of this top spot and how he plans on playing this week when he tees it up with the pros at the 3M Open. And with 3 weeks left until the PGA TOUR’s regular season wraps up, we’ll discuss five players who are in and around the top-70 of the FedExCup Standings and break down their chances of making it to the postseason.

This Is Why You Struggle To Spray Snow The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton break down why Robertson chose a short-term deal, whether he'll remain in Dallas beyond next season, and how the Stars could approach his next contract.

The guys also discuss the massive arbitration gap between the Columbus Blue Jackets and goaltender Jet Greaves, Connor Bedard's new contract with the Chicago Blackhawks, and the latest offseason storylines surrounding Dylan Larkin, Morgan Rielly, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes and Nikita Kucherov.

Later, New Jersey Devils goaltender Jake Allen joins the show to discuss preparing for a larger workload next season, the evolution of NHL goaltending, Canada's pipeline of elite goalies, three-goalie systems becoming more common around the league, his experience working Hockey Night in Canada, and the players who surprised him most in practice throughout his NHL career.

videos.title: How Loose Should My Muscles Be For Hockey?
videos.summary_source_text:
How Loose Should My Muscles Be For Hockey? Looseness is a trained skill, and it's the reason the smartest players on the ice tend to also be the smoothest.

When you're tense, your muscles are all working against each other, where the movers are firing while the muscles that should be resting fire right alongside them, and that wasted effort is one of the clearest things separating a beginner from an elite mover. 

The best athletes in any profession have trained that unnecessary tension out, which is why their movement looks effortless even while they're going faster than everyone around them.

This is where it gets interesting, because your brain only has so much bandwidth in any given moment. When your motor system is working overtime just to keep you upright and moving, it eats up the resources you'd otherwise spend reading the ice. Relaxed, efficient movement quiets that demand, and the attention and working memory it frees up is the exact thing we call hockey sense: seeing the play develop, holding your options in your head.

It also explains why some players shrink in big games. Under pressure you tense up, a skill you've drilled a thousand times suddenly needs conscious control again, your focus turns inward onto your own feet, and you stop seeing the ice. Same player, less looseness, and the game speeds up around them.

The catch is you can't just tell yourself to relax in the middle of a shift. Looseness has to be built into the mechanics themselves so it holds up when the speed and the pressure climb, and that's the whole reason we teach efficient movement first in the Downhill Skating System, so your brain is free to read the game instead of managing your feet.

videos.title: Episode 52: The Dog Days | Tri-State Hockey Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Episode 52: The Dog Days | Tri-State Hockey Podcast Jonny Lazarus, Arthur Staple and Mike Rupp are back together for Episode 52 of the Tri-State Hockey Podcast to assess where the New Jersey Devils, New York Rangers and New York Islanders stand following their offseason moves.

The guys begin with the Devils and debate whether New Jersey has the strongest roster of the three teams. They break down where Anthony Mantha could fit alongside Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt, the improved versatility of the forward group, concerns surrounding the defence and whether Jake Allen, Nico Daws and David Rittich can provide enough stability in goal.

The conversation then shifts to the Rangers following an active offseason. Arthur explains why he liked Chris Drury’s moves, while the group discusses the Vincent Trocheck trade, Pavel Dorofeyev, the Rangers’ lack of depth down the middle and the pressure facing J.T. Miller, Alexis Lafrenière, Gabe Perreault and head coach Mike Sullivan.

Finally, the guys examine the Islanders’ quiet summer, Anthony Duclair’s future, whether veteran players could block opportunities for younger talent and what Peter DeBoer can get out of the current roster. They also discuss the Islanders’ struggling power play, Matthew Schaefer’s role and whether the team did enough to improve. The show closes with a Tri-State trivia challenge featuring every Rangers, Islanders and Devils player to record a 30-goal season since 2003-04.

videos.summary_source_text:
GPT 6 The 4 TRILLION Parameter Reset Nobody Expected Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
OpenAI is now seven releases deep into the GPT-5 generation, yet there is still no official GPT-6 announcement, model card, or confirmed release date.

In this video, we examine what may be happening behind the scenes at OpenAI—from the reported government review connected to GPT-5.6 and the alleged scrapping of the original GPT-6 “Spud” training run to the scheduled retirement of GPT-5.4.

The bigger question is not whether GPT-5.6 is capable. It is whether OpenAI is losing momentum, certainty, and release-cadence credibility while Anthropic, xAI, and Google continue advancing their own frontier AI models.

We break down:

• Why GPT-5.6 reportedly faced an external government review
• Why seven GPT-5 releases have arrived without GPT-6
• What the reported “Scrapped Spud” reset could mean
• Why GPT-5.4’s retirement matters
• How OpenAI compares with Claude, Grok, and Gemini
• What developers building on the OpenAI API should do now
• Why frontier AI models are becoming harder to release on schedule
• What we still do—and do not—know about GPT-6

Is OpenAI genuinely falling behind, or is the entire AI industry discovering that the next generational leap requires more time, money, scrutiny, and uncertainty?

Share your GPT-6 release-date prediction in the comments.

Gemini 3.6 Flash Is Here — Google’s 3 New Models vs Claude and OpenAI Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
Google just launched three new Gemini AI models in a single afternoon: Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and the restricted-access Flash Cyber.

But while Gemini 3.6 Flash is designed to become Google’s new fast, affordable AI workhorse—and Flash-Lite targets high-volume, low-cost applications—the most interesting model may be the one almost nobody is allowed to use.

In this video, we break down Google’s three-model AI launch and separate confirmed facts from launch-day hype. We examine the claimed coding and agentic improvements in Gemini 3.6 Flash, explain who Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is really designed for, and investigate why Flash Cyber is restricted to sensitive government and cybersecurity work.

We also look at the bigger AI race involving Google, Claude, and OpenAI—and why major AI labs are increasingly creating locked-down cyber models that cannot be independently tested or benchmarked.

The launch generated serious attention, including coverage reportedly reaching more than 1,500 views per hour and search estimates of approximately 17,700 monthly US searches for Gemini 3.6 Flash. But popularity is not proof of performance.

Watch before switching models or believing the biggest Gemini headlines.

videos.title: What is the Purpose of Stress?
videos.summary_source_text:
What is the Purpose of Stress? What Is the Purpose of Stress?

Most of us think of stress as the enemy. But what if stress is actually your body's way of preparing you for action?

In this clip, neuroscientist @lfeldmanbarrett explains that stress isn't a design flaw. It's an evolutionary adaptation. Your brain is preparing your body for a big metabolic demand. Thousands of years ago that might have meant hunting, gathering, or escaping danger. Today it might mean a difficult meeting, parenting, or hours of focused knowledge work.

The chemistry hasn't changed. Our environment has.

One practical takeaway: when you feel stressed, move. Go for a walk. Practice yoga. Lift weights. Stretch. Give your body the physical outlet it's preparing for, instead of getting stuck in rumination and overthinking.

Thanks to @lfeldmanbarrett for helping us better understand why our brains and bodies respond to stress the way they do.

videos.summary_source_text:
Chip Like a Pro | Part 2 | Padraig Harrington As part of my YouTube series  “Ten lessons every golfer should know”, the sixth Paddy’s Golf Tip is on chipping, which is in two parts. 
 
In this second and final instalment,  I provide some insights on chipping, including judging where to land the ball on the green having assessed the risk attached and why practising putting from off the greens can be a useful option.  In addition, I highlight why using one specific club for all chips, until it is clearly not the right club, can be effective.

I also offer a tip for practising on the course using a number of balls, which can provide useful feedback and ultimately help get the ball "up and down"!

Because real learning happens when the body has time to sense what it is doing.
Many people try to improve movement through more effort, more repetition, and more correction. But if the body is already bracing or protecting, trying harder may only repeat the same pattern.
In this video, I explain why slow movement helps the nervous system recognize old patterns and discover new possibilities. You’ll also experience a short somatic exploration with gentle head turning.

There’s a three-year window in every woman’s life when she can lose more muscle than during the previous 20 years combined. Even with plenty of protein and regular exercise, many women still experience postmenopausal muscle loss.

Leucine is an essential amino acid that signals your muscles to grow. As you age, your protein and leucine requirements increase, making both especially important for maintaining muscle after menopause.

After menopause, estrogen levels drop significantly, contributing to postmenopausal muscle loss. Fortunately, exercise can help rebuild muscle. Research has shown that weight training can significantly improve muscle loss after menopause while also supporting bone health.

Age-related muscle loss is known as sarcopenia. It affects not only muscle tissue but also the nervous system and connective tissue, making it more difficult to rebuild muscle over time. This is why it’s important to begin preserving and rebuilding muscle as early as possible.

21.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

AJ Jones Has The Most Iconic Trick Shot On Golf Social Media | Closed Course Welcome back to another episode of Closed Course!

The guys are back with another great interview, this time catching up with golf trick-shot master AJ Jones. From long drive competitions to viral golf social media videos, AJ has built a phenomenal following in the golf community through his unique approach to growing a love for the game. A former Division I baseball player at Long Beach State University, AJ transitioned into golf content creation after his collegiate career. He credits his baseball background for the incredible trick shots that require elite hand-eye coordination. AJ's brand isn't just about golf, either. Much of his content is centered around charity work and giving back to the community.

From his iconic stinger trick shot to his time and accolades as a professional long driver, this interview with AJ is a must-listen for golf fans.

You can find AJ on Instagram and TikTok @ajjonesgolf, and you can visit his website at ajjonesgolf.com.

He credits his baseball background for the incredible trick shots that require elite hand-eye coordination. AJ's brand isn't just about golf, either. Much of his content is centered around charity work and giving back to the community.

From his iconic stinger trick shot to his time and accolades as a professional long driver, this interview with AJ is a must-listen for golf fans.

You can find AJ on Instagram and TikTok @ajjonesgolf, and you can visit his website at ajjonesgolf.com.

After wrapping things up with AJ, the guys get into some general golf talk, including the Korn Ferry Tour and how more celebrities are starting to get into the game, including Justin Gaethje.
Tune in to the Closed Course podcast every Tuesday at 6:00 a.m. for great golf conversations and unforgettable interviews with all sorts of unique guests.

videos.summary_source_text:
This Is Why You Struggle To Grip The Ice The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Bedard signs his extension & Greaves arbitration filing ft. Greg Wyshynski & Jack Campbell
videos.summary_source_text:
Bedard signs his extension & Greaves arbitration filing ft. Greg Wyshynski & Jack Campbell On today’s episode of The Sheet, Jeff Marek is joined by Greg Wyshynski of ESPN. The big news of the weekend, Connor Bedard signing a 5 year, $15M AAV extension with Chicago. Jeff and Greg discuss that deal, the intricacies hidden in it, and what it means for the Blackhawks 5 year outlook.

They also dive into this morning's news of Jet Greaves arbitration filings. The young netminder and the Columbus Blue Jackets remain millions of dollars apart. Will they figure out a deal in the next 48 hours, or will an arbitrator have to decide whether Greaves is paid like a young backup goalie or a legit number one? Wysh also shares his thoughts on the NHL's evolving regional sports network saga and the league's broadcast bootcamp that took place recently.

Finally, we welcome former Dallas Stars, LA Kings, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Edmonton Oilers goaltender Jack Campbell to the show. Jack recently announced his retirement from hockey. He opens up about his mental health struggles, how he persevered through them, and what his post-playing career will look like.

"Inget slår min Koenigsegg Jesko, men jag behöver andra sportbilar!" Ronnie Gustafsson lägger inte upp något på sociala medier, men för två år sedan fick jag intervjua honom om hans Koenigsegg CCXR – och det är min mest sedda film med 300 000 visningar.
Nu har jag fått en till exklusiv intervju på den fantastiska bilutställningen The Aurora, där Ronnie visade upp tio av sina favoritbilar, som bjöd på en "Bilsymfoni!"
Inget överskuggar hans Jesko, som han redan har hunnit köra på bana med två gånger och ska lära sig göra 360-svängar med. En bil för runt 35 miljoner …
Men i samlingen finns bilar som är magiska på andra vis. 
Vi snackar körglädje, bilutveckling, varför Jeskon har fått en alldeles speciell grön färg, favoriter, bilkörning, bankörning, restomods, familjen Koenigsegg, elbilar och om den tredje Koenigsegg han beställt …
Jag har en stående inbjudan till hans garage, där hela samlingen finns! Så det kommer mera längre fram.
Stort tack!

Who makes the STRONGEST engines? Merc v Toyota v Land Rover We test the strength and reliability of an old Toyota Land Cruiser, Land Rover Discovery and Mercedes ML by running the cars at full throttle for as long as possible. 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-21-07

Who builds the strongest engines - Toyota, Land Rover, or Mercedes? 

Well, to find out, we’re pushing our £2,000 Toyota Land Cruiser, Land Rover Discovery and Mercedes ML to the limit to see which lasts the longest. 

They’re no longer road-worthy, but which can last the longest when pushed to full throttle?  First off, let’s take a closer look at the contenders: 

Starting with the Discovery 3, it’s powered by a 2.7-litre V6 that produces 190hp and 440Nm. It’s equipped with a 6-speed manual and weighs 2,419kg. It was first released in 2005, we bought it for £1,500, and it currently has 256,000 miles on the clock. 

Up next is the Mercedes ML. There’s a 2.7-litre inline-5 turbo diesel under the bonnet, and this produces 163hp and 400Nm. It’s equipped with a 5-speed automatic gearbox, weighs around 2,100kg, and was released in 2005. We bought it for £1,800, and it has 140,000 miles on the clock. 

Finally, we come to the Land Cruiser. It’s powered by a 4.7-litre V8, and this puts down 235hp and 434Nm. It rolls up with a 4-speed automatic gearbox, and it weighs 2,260kg. It was originally released in 2002, and although it was originally bought for £5,000, it’s only worth around £2,000 now. To date, it’s run around 282,000 miles.

videos.title: Rotera med en mening…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Rotera med en mening… Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till lär dig rotera med en mening. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook. Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

videos.title: 20.07.26 - HIP-4 Explained: The Future of Prediction Markets on Hyperliquid
videos.summary_source_text:
20.07.26 - HIP-4 Explained: The Future of Prediction Markets on Hyperliquid Welcome to Bonus Episode 3 of the RIFT Before You Quit series on Predictions market.

In this special technical deep dive, we explore HIP-4 (Hyperliquid Improvement Proposal 4) and how it forms the foundation for the next generation of on-chain prediction markets inside the RIFT ecosystem.

Prediction markets are much more than simple yes-or-no betting systems. They require sophisticated infrastructure capable of creating outcome contracts, matching buyers and sellers, managing collateral, recording ownership, resolving real-world events, and distributing payouts transparently. This episode explains how Hyperliquid's HIP-4 framework provides that infrastructure and why it represents a major advancement in decentralized financial markets.

Topics covered include:

- What HIP-4 is and why it was created
- How prediction markets differ from perpetual futures trading
- The importance of fully collateralized outcome contracts
- Why outcome markets require specialised blockchain infrastructure
- Binary markets, range markets and multi-outcome contracts
- How outcome shares are created, traded and settled
- Understanding market probabilities through pricing
- Order books within prediction markets
- Event resolution and transparent settlement mechanisms
- How collateral protects participants
- Why prediction markets cannot rely on simple web interfaces alone
- The role of smart contracts in automated settlement
- Market liquidity and capital efficiency
- Risk management within outcome-based trading
- How prediction market contracts are represented on Hyperliquid
- Why bounded outcomes create predictable maximum risk
- The technical differences between prediction markets and leveraged derivatives
- How traders can enter and exit positions before final settlement
- Why prediction markets are active trading markets rather than traditional wagering systems
- The importance of trusted data sources and objective event resolution
- Infrastructure required to support decentralized prediction markets at scale

The episode also explains why RIFT chose to build its prediction market framework on Hyperliquid's HIP-4 infrastructure rather than developing an entirely separate settlement engine. By leveraging specialised protocol-level functionality, RIFT can focus on delivering an intuitive trading experience while benefiting from transparent on-chain execution, efficient order matching and secure settlement.

You'll also gain an understanding of how prediction markets may eventually integrate with the wider RIFT ecosystem, including Smart Money, automated trading infrastructure, market intelligence tools and future AI-powered trading systems.

Whether you're new to prediction markets or want to understand the technology powering one of RIFT's newest features, this episode provides a comprehensive introduction to the mechanics, architecture and future potential of decentralized outcome markets.

As blockchain technology continues to evolve, prediction markets are expected to become an increasingly important component of decentralized finance, allowing participants to trade on real-world events through transparent, fully collateralized and non-custodial infrastructure.

Hindi - 20.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: Rotate with a purpose…
videos.channel: Better & Easier golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
Rotate with a purpose… Everything we do should have a proper purpose and rotation without a good reason is just stupid. Rotation should happen to support how you want to move the club. 

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro to how to rotate with a purpose in an effortless golf swing. 

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

A will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

Christie was an athletic golfer, but her driver swing was getting steep and working a little over the top. The main reason was her lower body was swaying, which left her upper body leading the downswing and caused the club to cut across the ball.

In this lesson, we worked on stabilising the lower body, improving her position at the top, and then using the lower body to lead the downswing. Once her body sequence improved, the club started to shallow, her path became more neutral, and her drives started flying much straighter.

If your driver swing gets steep, you come over the top, or you struggle to stop cutting across the ball, this lesson will show you how the body can help create a better downswing without forcing the club into position.

videos.title: Your Diet Programs Your Baby
videos.summary_source_text:
Your Diet Programs Your Baby Science shows that what you eat during pregnancy may influence how your baby’s genes behave for the rest of their life. How crazy is that.

Scientists call this epigenetics. Think of it like dimmer switches sitting on top of your DNA. These switches can turn certain genes on or off depending on the environment in the womb.

Nutrients, stress, sleep, and metabolic health all send messages about what kind of world the baby should prepare for.

This is powerful because it shows that parents may have influence long before birth. Small daily choices may help build a stronger foundation for brain development, metabolism, and lifelong health.

This is why I wrote a book all about pregnancy nutrition. It's called 9 Months That Count Forever and contains all the science and easy practical tips I used during my own pregnancy.

videos.summary_source_text:
Jaecoo 8 Review: PROOF German SUVs are overpriced! This is our in-depth review of the Jaecoo 8 SUV. We’ll run you through the design, the interior, what it’s like to drive, and test its acceleration from 0mph to 60mph.

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

This is the all-new Jaecoo 8! 

It’s a competitor to renowned, established family SUVs like the Skoda Kodiaq and Hyundai Santa Fe. The question is, does this all-new Chinese competitor have what it takes to overcome them? Let’s take a closer look… 

Starting with the design, it’s fair to say Jaecoo seems to have taken some inspiration from Audi! The shape and size of the grille, coupled with the headlight design, look to have been lifted from an Audi Q7! The vertical slats within the grille also seem incredibly similar to what recent Mercedes SUVs have to offer. Around the back, there’s a full-length light bar, a roof spoiler, and the brand’s name is embossed across the boot - as seen in almost every new car these days! All in all, it looks like a premium car from whatever angle you look at it. 

Step inside, and it seems Jaecoo has once again taken inspiration from another brand - but this time it’s Mercedes instead of Audi! The positioning of the vents, buttons and drive selector stalks all seem similar to what you’ll find in a Mercedes, even if the quality is a bit lower down the pecking order. There’s a relatively large infotainment screen and digital dial display which serve their purpose well enough, and the cabin is relatively well built. There’s also a good amount of storage throughout. 

The Jaecoo 8 is powered by a 1.5-litre hybrid petrol engine that can deliver 428hp. This powers the front wheels, and it can accelerate to 60mph in just 5.8 seconds. 

The Jaecoo 8 starts from just £45,500, so it’s relatively in line with competitors like the Santa Fe. The thing is, whereas top-of-the-range models of the Santa Fe increase up to around £60,000, there aren’t various different trims to consider with the Jaecoo - all models come with the same features and tech!

So would you be ready to choose this 7-seater over its rivals? Stick with Mat to see if you should!

videos.title: Why Women in 50s Have Shoulder Problems?
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Women in 50s Have Shoulder Problems? Why do so many women get frozen shoulder in their 50s? 

One of the biggest reasons appears to be the hormonal changes that happen during perimenopause and menopause.

When estrogen drops, it sets off a cascade of changes:

• Inflammation tends to increase.
• The shoulder becomes more prone to fibrosis (excess scar tissue), which can limit movement.
• Blood sugar regulation often gets worse, leading to more advanced glycation end products (AGEs), which can increase inflammation and make connective tissue stiffer.

Put all of that together, and it's not surprising that frozen shoulder is so common in women between 45 and 60.

The good news? 

Frozen shoulder is usually temporary.

For most people, it takes 1 to 3 years to resolve, but with patience, smart movement, and a progressive rehab program, there's a very good chance you'll regain most or all of your shoulder motion.

The biggest mistake is assuming it's your new normal.

It usually isn't.

videos.summary_source_text:
474. Rikedomskiftet för ett rikare liv: fyra faser och sex förflyttningar | Med Moa Diseborn Vilka är skiftena på den ekonomiska resan? Vilka är fällorna de flesta hamnar i? Vad händer när mer pengar inte förändrar vardagen i någon större omfattning? Det är frågan bakom Moas modell "The Wealth Shift". Avsnittet blev ärligt talat också mer personligt än jag hade tänkt från början eftersom jag insåg tydligt var jag själv fortfarande sitter fast. 

Moa har kokat ner alla år vi jobbat med de här frågorna till en egen modell med fyra faser (get rich, stay rich, live rich, leave rich) och sex tankeskiften man behöver rör sig genom längs den ekonomiska resan och när pengarna väl finns där.

Det handlar om att gå från ett bristtänk till att våga tänka att det finns tillräckligt, från prestation och nyttovärde till identitet, från att samla på hög till att veta vad man faktiskt vill. Och det viktigaste: de flesta av skiftena går att börja med oavsett var du står ekonomiskt.

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt:
• Varför vi nästan aldrig pratar om vad som händer när pengarna väl finns där
• De fyra faserna: get rich, stay rich, live rich och leave rich
• Från brist till tillräckligt, och varför "nästa miljon" aldrig räcker
• Från prestation till identitet: vem du är när du inte längre behöver bevisa något
• Från ackumulering till avsikt, när nästa miljon tappar sin lockelse
• Ensamheten som kan följa med framgång, och vägen till tillhörighet
• Från framgång till bidrag: vad du vill förstärka i världen
• Arv som något du lever redan i dag, inte bara lämnar efter dig

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan, Caroline och Moa Diseborn
